gravity.description: Default { x: 0, y: 1 } — Matter's own 'earth gravity' unit (scaled internally by engine.gravity.scale, default 0.001), tuned for pixel-space worlds out of the box.

gravityScale.description: Override for engine.gravity.scale. Leave unset to use Matter's default (0.001).

iterations.description: Matter constraint/position/velocity solver iterations. Default: Matter's own default (6).

startFrame.description: Scene-local frame the simulation begins stepping at. Every frame before this holds all dynamic bodies at their initial resolved position (pre-drop).

bodyType.description: 'dynamic': simulated — falls/bounces under gravity and collisions, and gets a baked resolvedPhysics.frames[] track. 'static': an immovable anchor other bodies can collide with (a ledge, floor, wall); never moves regardless of gravity, and gets NO resolvedPhysics track — it renders at its normal resolvedPosition, unchanged. Note: shape: 'path' requires bodyType: 'static'.

pathSegments.description: Only used with shape:'path'. Number of straight sub-segments the resolved curve (asset.content._path, e.g. a WavyLine) is chopped into to approximate a collision surface — Matter has no native bezier body. Higher = smoother collisions, more bodies.

radius.description: Circle radius in px. Only used when shape is 'circle'; defaults to min(width,height)/2.

frictionAir.description: Air resistance. 0 lets a dynamic body fall/slide forever without damping.

initialVelocity.description: px/frame at simulation start. Default { x: 0, y: 0 }.

fixedRotation.description: Body never rotates (infinite inertia) — e.g. a card that should slide/bounce but stay upright.

collidesWith.description: Asset ids (same scene) this body may collide with. Omit to collide with every other physics body in the scene (default).

vector.description: Acceleration in px/frame² — the SAME units as initialVelocity, deliberately NOT Matter's mass-scaled applyForce() API, so this stays predictable and composes cleanly with gravity/initialVelocity instead of needing a separate mental model.

oneShot.description: true: applied once, as an instantaneous velocity kick, at startFrame — a shove. false (default): applied every simulated frame within [startFrame, endFrame) — a sustained push, e.g. wind.

endFrame.description: Scene-local frame the continuous force stops (exclusive). Omit to apply for the rest of the simulation. Ignored when oneShot is true.

targetAssetId.description: Another asset id in this scene that ALSO carries a `physics` block (dynamic or static — a static anchor is the common case, e.g. an invisible marker placed where you want the body to climb toward). This body accelerates toward that target's live simulated position every step.

strength.description: Attraction acceleration, px/frame². This is the energy source that can make a body climb — gravity+friction alone never will.

falloff.description: 'none': constant pull regardless of distance (predictable, recommended for a deliberate 'climb to this point' effect). 'linear'/'quadratic': weaker the farther away.

maxDistance.description: Only pulls within this px distance of the target. Omit for unlimited range.

endFrame.description: Scene-local frame the pull stops (exclusive). Omit to pull for the rest of the simulation.

attractTo.description: 'centroid' (default, unchanged): pull toward the target body's center of mass. 'nearestSurfacePoint': pull toward the closest point on the target's boundary — for a rectangle/circle this is the nearest edge point; for a shape:'path' target (e.g. a WavyLine used as a magnet anchor), this is the nearest point on the actual curve, sampled from content._path, not the compound body's misleading centroid.

sceneId.description: An EARLIER scene (in manifest.scenes order) whose matching physics asset's FINAL baked frame — position, angle, and finite-differenced velocity — seeds this asset's initial simulation state, instead of starting from anchor/initialVelocity at rest. This is a resolve-time simulation-state carry, distinct from transitionOut.params.carryAssetId (which only passes resolvedPosition/resolvedStyle to the transition component for a visual crossfade during the cut, and never touches physics).

assetId.description: Asset id within sceneId to carry from. Defaults to this asset's own id — the common case: same logical coin, same id, in both scenes.
